title: Undercover Deadpool: Ryan Reynolds Roams Comic-Con Incognito, Takes Selfies with Unsuspecting Fans
summary: In a move that perfectly channels his alter ego's mischievous spirit, Ryan Reynolds pulled off an epic Comic-Con surprise. The actor donned a gray denim Deadpool suit — a far cry from the iconic red — and strolled the convention floor completely incognito. Fans posed for selfies with who they thought was an impressive cosplayer, only to later realize they'd met the real Merc with a Mouth. Reynolds captured the adventure on video, later posting, "No handlers, no security, no ropes. WHAT A GIFT." He described feeling "so lucky" to be among the devoted fans whose passion brought Deadpool to life a decade ago. The stunt culminated when he casually walked into the Marvel Studios presentation. Robert Downey Jr. spotted him and quipped, "Who's this guy with the swords and stuff?" Reynolds, playing along, replied, "Long-time listener, first-time caller." The actor has been dropping hints about Deadpool's future. While he confirmed there will "eventually" be another film, he envisions the character as a supporting player rather than the lead. "He is a guy who is great in a group," Reynolds said. He's also keen to mine "deep cuts" from the comics by writers like Fabian Nicieza and Gerry Duggan. Following the massive success of Deadpool & Wolverine, Reynolds revealed he's already started writing, but the antihero won't be the main focus. For now, his Comic-Con caper is a reminder of why fans adore him: he's as irreverent and unpredictable as the character he plays.
why_it_matters: Reynolds's stunt shows how actors can use surprise and humor to connect directly with fans in an age of social media, bypassing traditional PR. For young audiences, it highlights how a performer's personality can amplify a character's appeal, influencing how movies are marketed and how franchises stay alive between releases.

background_read: Comic-Con International in San Diego is the world's largest pop culture convention, where studios reveal upcoming movies and TV shows to thousands of fans. Ryan Reynolds, the actor who has portrayed the wisecracking antihero Deadpool since 2016, is famous for his viral marketing stunts.

His surprise appearance in a gray Deadpool suit was an homage to a lesser-known comic costume. Earlier this year, Deadpool & Wolverine, co-starring Hugh Jackman, became one of the highest-grossing R-rated films ever. Reynolds often credits comic writers Fabian Nicieza and Gerry Duggan for shaping Deadpool's voice.
Now, he's teasing a future where Deadpool might join other Marvel heroes in group adventures, mining 'deep cuts' from the comics rather than retreading familiar ground.

perspectives.description: Fans loved the playful homage; it strengthened the bond between Reynolds and Deadpool devotees, showing genuine appreciation for the community and keeping the character's mischievous spirit alive.

Some might argue the stunt is a clever distraction from the fact that Deadpool's solo film future is uncertain. Being relegated to a supporting role could dilute the character's unique edge and independence.

This stunt reflects modern celebrity marketing where spontaneous-appearing moments are often carefully filmed and edited for viral success, blurring the line between authentic interaction and a brand-building exercise.

Reynolds's hint at 'deep cuts' suggests the Deadpool franchise could explore more obscure comic storylines. This may please hardcore fans but risks alienating casual viewers if the references are too niche.
